source_reviews.independent_solution: Split one light beam into two propagation paths and recombine them; the two parts retain the same frequency and a stable phase difference. Equal frequencies alone do not establish coherence; independently emitting lamps normally have a varying relative phase.

Interference is the superposition of light-wave oscillations, enhancing light in some regions and weakening it in others. A stable fringe pattern requires coherence. Destructive superposition redistributes energy propagation rather than destroying light energy or necessarily converting it into heat.

The color distinction of monochromatic light is associated with frequency. At a stationary interface f is unchanged while v and wavelength can change, with v=f*lambda; wavelengths in different media alone therefore cannot identify a color change.

If an ice crack contains a sufficiently thin air gap and suitable illumination supplies two reflected beams that overlap, different frequencies interfere differently as gap thickness and optical path vary, giving colored reflections. This explains a possible observation, not every crack or a need to produce cracks. Ice-air-ice does not have the coating's two identical reflection phase reversals, so the air-film-glass quarter-wave antireflection rule cannot be transferred directly.

No. For water relative to air, v_water=v_air/n and lambda_water=lambda_air/n, while f=v/lambda stays unchanged. Wavelength shortening does not remove visible frequencies or imply inability to see surrounding illuminated objects. It is not a claim of perfect visibility in all water.

Main applications here are interferometric measurement of wavelength or gas refractive index, surface-quality inspection through bending interference fringes in a wedge-shaped air layer, and antireflection treatment by thin-film interference. At normal incidence with n_air<n_film<n_glass, both reflected waves reverse phase equally; 2h=lambda_film/2 gives h=lambda_vacuum/(4*n_film). Complete cancellation also needs equal amplitudes. One green-light design does not cancel every color, and full transmission additionally needs the transparent, nonabsorbing, no-other-loss ideal model.
